items.explain: The pawn strike ...c5 is the engine's top move. ...e5 is playable and masters choose it often, but it scores about a third of a pawn lower (depth 16): after d5 the c-pawn can no longer strike at d4.

feedback_by_move.e7e5: Playable, and masters choose it often, but the engine scores it at least 30 cp below ...c5 (depth 16): after d5 the c5 strike is gone.

items.explain: ...c5 is the engine's top move; ...e5, ...Bg4, ...Na6 and ...Re8 are within 40 cp at depth 16. The quiet moves ...Nbd7, ...e6 and ...a5 do nothing about e5 and score 0.6 to 0.8 pawn worse, because White's e5 push comes with tempo. Other moves may also be sound; the list holds the ones the engine rates closest.

feedback_by_move.b8d7: A developing move, but it lets White push e5 at once. It scores about 0.8 pawn worse than the best move (depth 16).
feedback_by_move.e7e6: This blocks Black's own bishop and does not strike the centre; e5 follows. It scores about 0.6 pawn worse (depth 16).
feedback_by_move.a7a5: A waiting move; White uses the time for e5. It scores about 0.6 pawn worse (depth 16).
